prompt.context_jp: 「もし何かあったら 責任___私___取る」
prompt.prompt_jp: もし何かあったら 責任___私___取る。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particles that fit the branch manager's assertion that HE (not anyone else) will be the one to take responsibility.

feedback.correct_en: 責任 is the topic being discussed (what happens if trouble arises), so は fits. 私が identifies exhaustively WHO takes it — 'I, and no one else.' This is a classic topic-は + exhaustive-が pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: Swapping to 責任が／私は would read as introducing 'responsibility' as new info while making '私' merely the general topic, losing the branch manager's emphatic self-nomination.

contrast_examples.en: As for responsibility, I'm the one who'll take it.
I will take responsibility. (plain statement, no exhaustive emphasis)

prompt.context_jp: 「約300人の 女性会員を集めておきながら 男性会員___1人も いなかった」
prompt.prompt_jp: 男性会員___1人もいなかったそうです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the contrastive focus against the 300 female members.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence sets up a sharp contrast: 300 female members WERE gathered, but male members — not a single one. は carries that contrastive 'as for X' flavor against the preceding clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report 'no male members existed' as new info, missing the deliberate juxtaposition with 女性会員. も would mean 'also none', which doesn't match the one-sided comparison.

contrast_examples.jp: 女性会員は多かったが、男性会員は一人もいなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Female members were many, but male members — not one.

contrast_examples.jp: 男性会員がいなかった。
contrast_examples.en: There were no male members. (neutral report)

prompt.context_jp: 「ハァ… 抗議文___送られてきたんだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 抗議文___送られてきたんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Souma is announcing fresh news to Mai. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is the first mention of 抗議文 in the conversation — brand-new information being presented. が introduces this fresh subject into Mai's awareness.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose that the protest letter was already a known topic. を doesn't fit with the passive verb 送られてきた.

contrast_examples.en: That letter did come. (already known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「ここ___お前ん家？」
prompt.prompt_jp: ここ___お前ん家？
prompt.prompt_en: Souma, surprised by the sign 「花咲」, is identifying THIS specific place. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Souma is performing exhaustive identification: 'THIS (of all places) is your house?' が picks out ここ as the answer to an implicit 'which place is it?'
feedback.incorrect_en: ここは would be a neutral topic ('As for here, it's your house?'), losing the astonished 'this is it?!' nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 「お父さん___人の話 全然 聞かないからでしょう！」
prompt.prompt_jp: お父さん___人の話 全然 聞かないからでしょう！
prompt.prompt_en: Mai is pinning the blame on Dad specifically. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: In a subordinate 〜から clause giving a reason, the subject is typically marked with が. Mai is also exhaustively identifying who is at fault: 'because YOU don't listen.'
feedback.incorrect_en: お父さんは would turn Dad into the main topic of the whole utterance, awkward inside a 〜から reason clause explaining the previous turn.

contrast_examples.jp: お父さんが聞かないからだ。

contrast_examples.en: Dad (as for him) doesn't listen. (standalone statement)

prompt.context_jp: 「そのなかで舞___、ふと自分の胸の奥___ざわつくのを感じ取っていた」
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞___、ふと自分の胸の奥___ざわつくのを感じ取っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particles that fit: Mai as topic + a new sensation welling up inside her.

feedback.correct_en: 舞 is the established scene topic (she's observing the wedding), so は. The 胸の奥がざわつく stirring is new, unexpected information bubbling up inside her — が marks it as a fresh phenomenon.
feedback.incorrect_en: 舞が would re-introduce Mai as if new; 胸の奥は would make the chest the topic, oddly contrasting it with something else.

contrast_examples.en: As for him, his chest ached. (topic + new sensation)

prompt.context_jp: 「塀の陰から様子をうかがうように、車のドアへ手を伸ばしている男___いる」
prompt.prompt_jp: 車のドアへ手を伸ばしている男___いる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing a figure Mai suddenly spots.

feedback.correct_en: Existential 〜がいる presents something newly perceived into the scene. Mai has just spotted the man; he's brand-new to the narrative moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: 男はいる would presuppose a known man and merely confirm his existence — not the moment of discovery the narration describes.

contrast_examples.en: That person is here/exists. (confirming known entity)

prompt.context_jp: 「染め抜かれた古びた暖簾をくぐり、幸三___ひょいと外へ出てきた」
prompt.prompt_jp: 幸三___ひょいと外へ出てきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. Kozo appears on the scene for the first time.

feedback.correct_en: Kozo enters the narrative here for the first time — a fresh appearance event. が marks the newly-introduced subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: 幸三は would treat Kozo as already-established topic, which clashes with his sudden entrance from inside the shop.

contrast_examples.en: Dad (as for him) came out. (dad as given topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「相馬健___上司の呼び出しを受け、机の前に静かに立っていた」
prompt.prompt_jp: 相馬健___上司の呼び出しを受け、机の前に静かに立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. Soma is being set up as the chapter's point-of-view.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence launches a paragraph about Soma — he's being established as the ongoing topic for the following clauses (standing, feeling unease, etc.). は fits topic-setting narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: 相馬健が would mark his action as new info within an already-ongoing scene, but here the narration is opening a new scene around him.

contrast_examples.jp: 田中は部屋に入り、椅子に座った。
contrast_examples.en: Tanaka entered the room and sat down. (topic chaining)
Tanaka came in. (new appearance in an ongoing scene)

prompt.context_jp: 「そこに名前のある313人 全員___な」
prompt.prompt_jp: そこに名前のある313人 全員___な。
prompt.prompt_en: Souma emphasizes that EVERY ONE of the 313 is in the same situation. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 全員が exhaustively picks out the entire set — 'all 313, every single one.' This matches the shocking revelation that nobody was introduced to anyone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 全員は would soften it to 'as for everyone', losing the emphatic 'ALL of them, without exception' punch.

contrast_examples.jp: 全員は賛成していない。

prompt.context_jp: 「コストを削減するために 女子行員___嫌がらせをして 辞めさせるなんて おかしいです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 女子行員___嫌がらせをして 辞めさせる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the target of the harassment.

feedback.correct_en: 嫌がらせをする takes に to mark the person on the receiving end of the harassment — the female staff are the target the action is directed at.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would mis-cast them as the direct object of some generic verb; the actual direct object slot is already taken by 嫌がらせ.

prompt.context_jp: 「社長___会員から集めた6億___持って 失踪したようです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 社長___会員から集めた6億___持って 失踪したようです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particles. The president is already in the shared context; the 600 million is the thing he took.

feedback.correct_en: 社長 has already been established — he's the known topic (は). 6億 is the direct object of 持って (took/carried off), hence を.
feedback.incorrect_en: 6億が would mis-mark the money as subject; 社長が would re-introduce a known entity as new.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は金を持って逃げた。
contrast_examples.en: He took the money and fled.

prompt.context_jp: 「君___ 支店長の私___ 逆らうつもりか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 君___ 支店長の私___ 逆らうつもりか？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particles for Nitta's intimidating question.

feedback.correct_en: 君 is addressed as topic (は). 逆らう takes に to mark whom you oppose/defy — 'defy ME, the branch manager.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 逆らう doesn't take を; it's an intransitive-style verb that pairs its target with に.

prompt.context_jp: 「ビンゴをそっと隠すように置いた亜紀の頬に、はにかんだ赤み___さす」
prompt.prompt_jp: 亜紀の頬に、はにかんだ赤み___さす。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. A blush suddenly appears on Aki's cheeks.

feedback.correct_en: 赤みがさす is a classic phenomenon-description: a blush appears as a newly-observed event. が marks the newly-emerging subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: 赤みは would presuppose a known blush and contrast it with something — nonsensical here.

contrast_examples.en: Stars are things that shine. (generic topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「…となると 当行___ 詐欺に手を 貸していたということになります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 当行___詐欺に手を貸していたということになります。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Mai's grave statement about 'our bank.'

feedback.correct_en: 当行 is being set up as the topic whose situation Mai is characterizing. は fits generic/characterizing statements about an established referent.
feedback.incorrect_en: 当行が would frame the bank as new information or exhaustive answer, odd when the whole conversation has been about the bank all along.

contrast_examples.jp: 当行はこの件に関与していない。
contrast_examples.en: Our bank is not involved in this matter. (characterizing)

prompt.context_jp: 「彼はこれから告げられる人事の中身___、かすかな不安を覚えていた」
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼はこれから告げられる人事の中身___、かすかな不安を覚えていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what Soma feels unease TOWARD.

feedback.correct_en: 〜に不安を覚える: the emotion is directed TOWARD a target with に. The direct object slot (を) is already filled by 不安.
feedback.incorrect_en: を can't double-mark here since 不安 is already the direct object. で would read as a location/means, not fitting an emotional target.

contrast_examples.en: Worry about the future. (を with 心配する)

prompt.context_jp: 「向こうが出してきた 事業計画書___基づいて審査した」
prompt.prompt_jp: 事業計画書___基づいて審査した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that pairs with 基づく (to be based on).

feedback.correct_en: 〜に基づく is a fixed grammatical pattern meaning 'based on 〜'. The に is lexically required by 基づく.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would read as a tool/location, not the 'basis' meaning. を doesn't fit 基づく at all.

contrast_examples.en: Write with a pen. (で as means)

prompt.context_jp: Mai pushes back politely-but-firmly at Soma's dismissive 'たかが窓口の仕事なのに':
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___を返すようですが…」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the set phrase Mai uses to signal a polite rebuttal.

feedback.correct_en: お言葉を返すようですが is a fixed polite preface meaning 'I hate to contradict you, but...' — the honorific お言葉 refers to the superior's just-spoken words.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other nouns don't form this idiom. 返事を返す / 話を返す are not fixed polite-disagreement openers.

contrast_examples.jp: お言葉を返すようですが、違うと思います。
お返事をお待ちしております。

prompt.context_jp: Soma warns Mai not to meddle at the branch they're inspecting:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「同じ銀行でも ___の会社だと思え」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the word meaning 'someone else's / an outside party's.'

feedback.correct_en: よそさま ('somebody else's', with honorific さま) is standard in business/polite speech to refer to an outside party. Soma is telling Mai to treat the branch as an outsider's turf.
feedback.incorrect_en: うちさま isn't a word; みなさま means 'everyone'; おたがい means 'each other'. None capture the 'other party / outside household' meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: よそさまに迷惑をかけるな。

prompt.context_jp: Mai, seeing Aki announce her own impending engagement:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私 完全に___てる…」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb meaning 'left behind / lagging behind' (in the race to marriage).

feedback.correct_en: 出遅れる means 'to get off to a late start / fall behind.' Mai is lamenting she's lagging in the marriage race compared to Mika and Aki.
feedback.incorrect_en: 出かける = go out; 出会う = encounter; 出直す = start over. None convey 'lagging behind.'

contrast_examples.en: I got a late start on job hunting.

prompt.context_jp: The section chief tasks Soma with investigating the loan:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「取り引きの経緯や 融資に問題がなかったかどうか ___きてくれるか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb meaning 'investigate / look into.'

feedback.correct_en: 調べる is the standard verb for investigating facts, records, or problems. Perfect for a bank fact-finding mission.
feedback.incorrect_en: 探す = search for a lost item/person; 見つける = find; 聞く = ask/hear. None cover a thorough inquiry into a transaction's history.

prompt.context_jp: Mai defends the fraud victims:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___てると 冷静な判断が できなくなることもありますから」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the verb describing the women's emotional state.

feedback.correct_en: 焦る = to be anxious/impatient/pressed for time — exactly the state that leads people to make bad choices. Soma even uses 焦って just prior in the dialogue.
feedback.incorrect_en: 怒る (angry), 困る (troubled), 疲れる (tired) don't match the specific 'rushed/panicked judgment' nuance Mai is describing.

contrast_examples.jp: 怒ると声が大きくなる。
contrast_examples.en: When angry, my voice gets loud.

prompt.context_jp: Nitta threatens Sugishita about the loan:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「このままだと 融資した5000万は___」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the banking verb meaning 'become a bad debt / go unrecovered.'

feedback.correct_en: 焦げ付く is finance jargon for a loan becoming unrecoverable — a 'bad debt.' Literally 'to get burnt stuck,' metaphorically used for loans you'll never get back.
feedback.incorrect_en: 焼ける = burn/toast (literal); 沈む = sink; 流れる = flow/fall through. None are the standard banking term for a non-performing loan.

prompt.context_jp: Sugishita explains his powerlessness:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「支店長が自分の意にそぐわない部下 ___ことなんて簡単ですから」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the slang-ish verb meaning 'to transfer away (as punishment).'

feedback.correct_en: 飛ばす in corporate-speak means to pack someone off to an undesirable post — a punitive transfer. The classic 'left-hand transfer' threat in Japanese business dramas.
feedback.incorrect_en: 送る is neutral (send), 追う means pursue, 捨てる means abandon — none capture the specific 'exile to a remote branch' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: I got shipped off to the regions.

prompt.context_jp: Soma reminisces nervously about a particular teller:
prompt.prompt_jp: 「1人 ___目に 遭わされたテラーがおりまして」
prompt.prompt_en: Fill in the adjective meaning 'awful / terrible' in the idiom 'put through a rough time.'

feedback.correct_en: えらい目に遭う is a set idiom meaning 'to have a rough/terrible time of it.' Here えらい means 'awful,' not 'great/respected.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 大きい目 / 重い目 / 強い目 aren't idiomatic for 'rough experience.' The fixed collocation requires えらい or ひどい.

contrast_examples.en: To go through a rough patch. (same pattern)

prompt.context_jp: Soma, surprised, asks whether this really is Mai's house (casual, between boss and young subordinate):
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Soma's astonished question in this casual moment?

choices.text: ここは あなたの家ですか？
ここが お前の家であらせられますか？

feedback.correct_en: お前ん家 (contraction of お前の家) with が for identification matches Soma's gruff, blunt boss-speak in a shocked moment. The actual line from the chapter.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is too polite/distanced for the boss–subordinate dynamic; (c) uses absurd archaic keigo that nobody says.

contrast_examples.jp: こちらがご自宅ですか？
contrast_examples.en: Is this your residence? (formal, to a client)

prompt.context_jp: Soma introduces himself to Mai's father on first meeting:
prompt.prompt_en: Which self-introduction fits a formal first meeting with someone's parent?

choices.text: はじめまして 相馬と申します
相馬 ちょっと寄らせてもらった

feedback.correct_en: はじめまして + 〜と申します is the standard humble self-intro to a stranger, especially an elder. Matches the respectful register Soma uses with Mai's father.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is far too casual for a first meeting with an elder; (c) is awkwardly familiar and uses wording that doesn't even introduce the name properly.

contrast_examples.jp: はじめまして、山田と申します。
contrast_examples.en: Nice to meet you, I'm Yamada. (polite intro)
I'm Yamada, pleased to meet you. (friends-only)

prompt.context_jp: Branch manager Nitta receiving the HQ inspection pair with a touch of sarcasm:
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits a stiff but outwardly polite senior greeting a visiting HQ team?

choices.text: 本部の臨店さんに わざわざ来てもらうとは恐縮だよ
本部の人がわざわざ来てくれてマジ助かる
本部の方々にわざわざお越しいただくなど恐縮至極に存じ奉ります

feedback.correct_en: The chapter's line balances polite 恐縮だよ (acknowledging the trouble) with the familiar だよ, fitting Nitta's senior-to-junior stance toward Soma.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is way too casual slang for a branch manager at work; (c) piles on archaic humble forms that sound like exaggerated parody, not real speech.

contrast_examples.jp: わざわざ来てもらって恐縮だよ。
contrast_examples.en: Sorry to make you come all the way. (senior to junior)

contrast_examples.jp: お越しいただきありがとうございます。
contrast_examples.en: Thank you for coming. (standard polite to equals/clients)

prompt.context_jp: Mai's outburst to the executive about Yajima's harassment:
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural for Mai's indignant outburst?

choices.text: 上司だからって… 部下の人生を壊すなんて 間違ってます！
上司なので 部下の人生を壊すのは 間違っていらっしゃいます
上司がだから 部下は人生を壊すなんて 間違ってます

feedback.correct_en: だからって ('just because...') is the natural idiomatic concessive for an emotional protest, and 〜なんて 間違ってます conveys indignation. This is exactly the chapter's line.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) oddly uses respectful いらっしゃいます to describe something being wrong — doesn't work for 'wrong.' (c) scrambles the subject marking and reads as broken Japanese.

contrast_examples.jp: 上司だからって、何でも許されるわけじゃない。
contrast_examples.en: Just because you're the boss doesn't mean anything goes.
Since you're my boss, I'll obey. (neutral/formal)

prompt.context_jp: Soma giving Mai a stern warning about on-site inspections:
prompt.prompt_en: Which version fits Soma's blunt, boss-to-newbie warning tone?

choices.text: 臨店先で余計なことは 絶対 言うな
臨店先で余計なことは 絶対におっしゃらないでください
臨店先で余計なことを 絶対 言わないでいただけませんでしょうか

feedback.correct_en: The plain-form imperative 言うな is appropriate for a stern senior warning a junior, and the は on 余計なこと marks it as the contrastive focus ('that stuff — don't say it').
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) uses respectful おっしゃる toward one's own subordinate, which is wrong. (c) is excessively humble, totally out of register for a boss giving an order.

contrast_examples.jp: 余計なことはおっしゃらないでください。
contrast_examples.en: Please refrain from saying unnecessary things. (polite, upward)
